paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: Visualization on the metric of answer correctness.
model_annotation: This 3D bar chart visualizes the accuracy of three large language models—Davinci-003, ChatGPT, and BARD—across four distinct logical reasoning categories: Inductive, Abductive, Deductive, and Mix. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, representing the proportion of correct answers. The horizontal plane displays the model names along the depth axis and the reasoning types along the width axis. Each colored bar corresponds to a model-reasoning pair, with height indicating accuracy and color gradient (blue to yellow) visually reinforcing magnitude. Davinci-003 shows moderate accuracy across all categories, with its highest performance in the Mix category (~0.7). ChatGPT performs notably lower in Inductive and Abductive reasoning (~0.3–0.4), but improves in Deductive and Mix (~0.5–0.6). BARD exhibits the highest overall accuracy, particularly excelling in Deductive and Mix reasoning, with bars reaching approximately 0.7–0.8. The chart suggests that model performance varies significantly by reasoning type, with BARD consistently outperforming the others, especially in more complex or mixed logical tasks.
